name: Boulware-Deser Black Hole
description: The spherical black hole of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity in five dimensions, which David Boulware and Stanley Deser found in 1985. The curvature squared term of string theory keeps its metric function finite at the centre and leaves a small mass with no horizon, and the same field equations have a second solution that approaches anti-de Sitter space.

history:
How does a black hole change when string theory corrects Einstein's equations? The first correction to his action is quadratic in the curvature, and a quadratic term generally gives the graviton a ghost for company [zwiebach1985, charmousis2009]. One combination escapes, $R^2 - 4R_{\mu
u}R^{\mu
u} + R_{\mu
uho\sigma}R^{\mu
uho\sigma}$, named for Gauss and Bonnet: Barton Zwiebach showed in 1985 that it is "ghost-free" in more than four dimensions [zwiebach1985]. Kornel Lanczos had met it in 1938 and called what he found "a remarkable property of the Riemann-Christoffel tensor in four dimensions": there the combination is a total derivative and drops out of the field equations [lanczos1938, glavan2020]. Terms of its family are the only ones that keep the field equations of second order, by David Lovelock's theorem of 1971, and in five dimensions the Gauss-Bonnet term is the only one beyond Einstein's own and a cosmological constant [lovelock1971, garraffo2008].¶David Boulware and Stanley Deser solved the corrected theory that same year for a static, spherically symmetric field [boulware1985]. The field equations are quadratic in the metric function, so they have two roots, $$f_\pm(r) = 1 +  rac{r^2}{2\ell^2}\left(1 \pm \sqrt{1 +  rac{4\ell^2r_0^2}{r^4}}ight)$$ in five dimensions, with $r_0$ a length set by the mass and $\ell$ a length set by the Gauss-Bonnet coupling [boulware1985, garraffo2008, torii2005]. With the minus sign the solution is "asymptotically Schwarzschild", and as $\ell 	o 0$ it becomes Frank Tangherlini's black hole of five dimensions [boulware1985, tangherlini1963, garraffo2008]. The same solutions came independently from James Wheeler, and in 1986 David Wiltshire gave them an electric charge [wheeler1986, wiltshire1986, torii2005].¶Turn the length $\ell$ up on Tangherlini's hole and the horizon moves in from $r_0$ to $r_h = \sqrt{r_0^2 - \ell^2}$, and a mass with $r_0 \le \ell$ has no horizon: its singularity is naked [torii2005, garraffo2008]. Among Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet black holes this least mass belongs to five dimensions alone [garraffo2008]. At the centre the metric function stops at the finite value $1 - r_0/\ell$ [torii2005, garraffo2008]. Tangherlini's runs off to minus infinity there [tangherlini1963]. The Kretschmann scalar still diverges, as $1/r^4$ where Tangherlini's grows as $1/r^8$, and Takashi Torii and Hideki Maeda, who sorted every case in 2005, called the divergence "milder" [torii2005].¶How long does such a hole live? Its temperature is $$T =  rac{\hbar c}{2\pi k_B}\, rac{r_h}{r_h^2 + 2\ell^2},$$ which falls to zero as the horizon shrinks, while Tangherlini's hole grows hotter without limit [garraffo2008, beroiz2007]. So a small hole has a positive specific heat and can sit in equilibrium with its surroundings, and Robert Myers and Jonathan Simon concluded in 1988 that it has "an infinite lifetime" [myers1988]. Those small holes are unstable: that was the finding of Martín Beroiz, Gustavo Dotti, and Reinaldo Gleiser in 2007 [beroiz2007]. Small gravitational perturbations grow on every hole with $r_0 < (1 + \sqrt{2})\,\ell$, and that range holds every hole with a positive specific heat, $r_h < \sqrt{2}\,\ell$ [beroiz2007].¶And the root with the plus sign? Without the mass it is anti-de Sitter space of radius $\ell$, in a theory whose action has no cosmological constant [boulware1985, garraffo2008]. Boulware and Deser called this branch unstable, "because the graviton becomes a ghost there", and concluded: "The theory solves its own cosmological problem" [boulware1985]. Eighteen years later Deser went back to it with Bayram Tekin, computed its energy, and found it positive [deser2003]. In 1985, they wrote, it was "erroneously concluded" that the energy of this branch was negative [deser2003]. In 2008 Christos Charmousis and Antonio Padilla agreed about the mass and found the branch unstable all the same: the ghost is there, a spherical black hole does not excite it, and "a binary system" would [charmousis2008].¶Lanczos's property keeps the Gauss-Bonnet term out of the field equations in four dimensions, and in 2020 Dražen Glavan and Chunshan Lin proposed a way around it: divide the coupling by $D - 4$, with $D$ the dimension of spacetime, then let $D 	o 4$ [glavan2020]. Boulware and Deser's formula comes through the limit with $r^3$ under the square root, and Glavan and Lin read from it a black hole in which a falling particle "never reaches" $r = 0$ [glavan2020]. Metin Gürses, Tahsin Çağrı Şişman, and Bayram Tekin asked the same year whether there is such a theory in four dimensions, and answered "No!" [gurses2020]. Part of the field equations, they showed, "always remains higher dimensional" [gurses2020]. The formula holds in four dimensions all the same: theories of a metric and a scalar field, built in 2020 to make the limit well defined, have it as their black hole [fernandes2022].

related.text: This black hole with the Gauss-Bonnet term switched off. At $\ell = 0$ the radical is $W = r^2$, the metric function is Tangherlini's $1 - r_0^2/r^2$, and the horizon is back at $r_0$ [boulware1985, garraffo2008].

The second root of the field equations with its mass taken out is anti-de Sitter space of radius $\ell$ in five dimensions. No cosmological constant stands in the action, and the Gauss-Bonnet coupling sets the curvature [boulware1985, garraffo2008].

Black holes of anti-de Sitter space with flat and hyperbolic horizons. Rong-Gen Cai found their counterparts in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity in 2002, with the same square root in the metric function [cai2002, charmousis2009].

A black hole fed by a stream of radiation, its mass a function of the advanced time $v$. Tsutomu Kobayashi let the mass of this hole depend on $v$ in the same way in 2005, in Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates, with a null fluid for the radiation [kobayashi2005].

String theory's correction to Maxwell's field, beside its correction to Einstein's gravity. The metric of Born and Infeld's point charge has a radical of the same kind, the square root of $r^4$ plus a constant, and David Wiltshire solved for both corrections together in 1988 [gibbonsrasheed1995, wiltshire1988].

coordinates.name: Hyperspherical

parameters.description: Mass radius, $r_0^2 = 8GM/(3\pi c^2)$ with $G$ Newton's constant in five dimensions, the horizon radius of Tangherlini's black hole of the same mass $M$
Gauss-Bonnet length, $\ell^2 = 2\alpha$ for the coupling $\alpha$ of the Gauss-Bonnet term. For $r_0 > \ell$ the horizon is the sphere $r_h = \sqrt{r_0^2 - \ell^2}$
The radical of the metric function, an area, with $W = r^2$ at $\ell = 0$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \psi, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\psi$, $\theta$, $\phi$ the angles of the 3-sphere. We write $W = \sqrt{r^4 + 4\ell^2r_0^2}$, in which the metric function is $1 - 2r_0^2/\left(r^2 + W\right)$, Tangherlini's $1 - r_0^2/r^2$ at $\ell = 0$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{2r_0^2\,r\left(r^2 + W - 2r_0^2\right)}{W\left(r^2 + W\right)^2}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{2r_0^2\,r}{W\left(r^2 + W - 2r_0^2\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r^2 + W - 2r_0^2\right)}{r^2 + W}\dot{\psi}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r^2 + W - 2r_0^2\right)\sin^2\psi}{r^2 + W}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r^2 + W - 2r_0^2\right)\sin^2\psi\sin^2\theta}{r^2 + W}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Mass radius, $r_0^2 = 8GM/(3\pi c^2)$ with $G$ Newton's constant in five dimensions, the horizon radius of Tangherlini's black hole of the same mass $M$
Gauss-Bonnet length, $\ell^2 = 2\alpha$ for the coupling $\alpha$ of the Gauss-Bonnet term. For $r_0 > \ell$ the horizon is the sphere $r_h = \sqrt{r_0^2 - \ell^2}$
The radical of the metric function, an area, with $W = r^2$ at $\ell = 0$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(u, r, \psi, \theta, \phi)$, with the retarded time $u = ct - r_*$ a length, where $dr_*/dr = \left(1 - 2r_0^2/\left(r^2 + W\right)\right)^{-1}$ and $r_* = 0$ at $r = 0$, and we write $W = \sqrt{r^4 + 4\ell^2r_0^2}$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{2r_0^2\,r\left(r^2 + W - 2r_0^2\right)}{W\left(r^2 + W\right)^2}\dot{u}^2 + \dfrac{4r_0^2\,r}{W\left(r^2 + W\right)}\dot{u}\dot{r} - \dfrac{r\left(r^2 + W - 2r_0^2\right)}{r^2 + W}\dot{\psi}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r^2 + W - 2r_0^2\right)\sin^2\psi}{r^2 + W}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r^2 + W - 2r_0^2\right)\sin^2\psi\sin^2\theta}{r^2 + W}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Mass radius, $r_0^2 = 8GM/(3\pi c^2)$ with $G$ Newton's constant in five dimensions, the horizon radius of Tangherlini's black hole of the same mass $M$
Gauss-Bonnet length, $\ell^2 = 2\alpha$ for the coupling $\alpha$ of the Gauss-Bonnet term. For $r_0 > \ell$ the horizon is the sphere $r_h = \sqrt{r_0^2 - \ell^2}$
The radical of the metric function, an area, with $W = r^2$ at $\ell = 0$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(v, r, \psi, \theta, \phi)$, with the advanced time $v = ct + r_*$ a length, where $dr_*/dr = \left(1 - 2r_0^2/\left(r^2 + W\right)\right)^{-1}$ and $r_* = 0$ at $r = 0$, and we write $W = \sqrt{r^4 + 4\ell^2r_0^2}$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{2r_0^2\,r\left(r^2 + W - 2r_0^2\right)}{W\left(r^2 + W\right)^2}\dot{v}^2 - \dfrac{4r_0^2\,r}{W\left(r^2 + W\right)}\dot{v}\dot{r} - \dfrac{r\left(r^2 + W - 2r_0^2\right)}{r^2 + W}\dot{\psi}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r^2 + W - 2r_0^2\right)\sin^2\psi}{r^2 + W}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r^2 + W - 2r_0^2\right)\sin^2\psi\sin^2\theta}{r^2 + W}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Hyperspherical, Anti-de Sitter Branch

parameters.description: Mass radius, $r_0^2 = 8GM/(3\pi c^2)$ with $G$ Newton's constant in five dimensions, the horizon radius of Tangherlini's black hole of the same mass $M$
Gauss-Bonnet length, $\ell^2 = 2\alpha$ for the coupling $\alpha$ of the Gauss-Bonnet term, and the radius of the anti-de Sitter space this branch approaches far away
The radical of the metric function, an area

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \psi, \theta, \phi)$ for the other root of the quadratic that fixes the metric function, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time. We write $W = \sqrt{r^4 + 4\ell^2r_0^2}$, in which the metric function is $1 + 2r_0^2/\left(W - r^2\right)$, the first branch's with $W \to -W$, and it grows as $r^2/\ell^2$ far away. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{2r_0^2\,r\left(W - r^2 + 2r_0^2\right)}{W\left(W - r^2\right)^2}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{2r_0^2\,r}{W\left(W - r^2 + 2r_0^2\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(W - r^2 + 2r_0^2\right)}{W - r^2}\dot{\psi}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(W - r^2 + 2r_0^2\right)\sin^2\psi}{W - r^2}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(W - r^2 + 2r_0^2\right)\sin^2\psi\sin^2\theta}{W - r^2}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0
